      <p>RESEARCH</p>
      <h2 id="research-front-title">Neural operators for control and optimization.</h2>
      <p>My Ph.D. work established a methodological base in decision-focused forecasting and constrained optimization for water-energy systems. At Cornell, I now study neural operators and use their learned solution maps in closed-loop control and constrained optimization.</p>
    </header>

        <h3>Neural operators for physical systems</h3>
        <p>These models learn maps between input functions and physical solution fields while representing boundary conditions and forcing terms explicitly.</p>
        <span class="vector-tag">CURRENT POSTDOCTORAL FOCUS</span>
      </article>
      <article class="vector-card">
        <span class="vector-number">02</span>
        <h3>Neural operators for control</h3>
        <p>I study how operator rollout errors propagate through a closed-loop controller and how the control objective should shape model training.</p>
        <div class="mini-equation">a → 𝒢<sub>θ</sub>(a) → u</div>
      </article>
      <article class="vector-card">
        <span class="vector-number">03</span>
        <h3>Neural operators in constrained optimization</h3>
        <p>I embed differentiable solution operators in constrained optimization and evaluate surrogate error through the decisions it changes.</p>
        <div class="mini-lattice" aria-hidden="true"><i></i><i></i><i></i><i></i><i></i><i></i></div>
      </article>
      <article class="vector-card">
        <span class="vector-number">04</span>
        <h3>Physical AI for materials processes</h3>

        <div class="uncertainty-strip" aria-hidden="true"><i></i></div>
